Sauti continued, 'O Brahmanas, O foremost one of Bhrigu's race, as thy ancestor Pramati had cheerfully narrated unto his inquiring son Ruru, and as I had heard it, thus have I recited this blessed history, from the beginning, of the learned Astika.
which thou hadst asked me about after hearing the story of the Dundubha

O son of a Suta! Recite therefore, all those to me fully.
Thou foremost of good men, recite it unto me, for, O son of a Suta, my thirst hath not been appeased by all thou hast said.
O Brahmana, listen to it in full, as I recite it.
But Vyasa recited the wonderful and great history called the Bharata.
the learned Rishi Krishna-Dwaipayana went thither on the occasion.
And he, the grand-father of the Pandavas, was born in an island of the Yamuna, of the virgin Kali by Sakti's son, Parasara.
Of sacred deeds and great fame, he begot Pandu and Dhritarashtra and Vidura in order to continue the line of Santanu.

they set fire to that house of lac and burnt Purochana (their enemy and the spy of Duryodhana) to death.

unresolved: Jaratkaru is identified only as the parent of Astika (ev_astika_parent); this batch does not resolve the parent's gender or distinguish possible homonymous Jaratkarus.
Kali and Satyavati are separately named in Vyasa's parentage (ev_vyasa_birth, ev_satyavati), but are not equated in this batch.

Kunti and Pritha are retained separately because their names are not equated in this batch. Collective references describe the Pandavas as sons of Kunti and sons of Pritha, while Nakula and Sahadeva are explicitly sons of Madri (ev_kunti_collective, ev_pritha_collective, ev_pritha_madri). The collective parent claims are recorded with unspecified parenthood; the text does not distinguish biological, adoptive or social roles.

The deceased father of the Pandavas is not named in ev_pandava_father. Pandu is separately named as a parent of Bhima and Arjuna (ev_vaka, ev_sachi_sri); the unnamed father has not been merged with Pandu.

Dhananjaya is called a Pandava but is not equated with Arjuna or another named individual (ev_dhananjaya). No identity among the five Pandavas, additional sixth member, or collective family and marriage relationships have been inferred for this unresolved name.

Vyasa's alias Krishna and Draupadi's alias Krishna denote distinct individuals. Krishna of Dwaravati and Dhananjaya's charioteer Krishna may denote the same individual, but this batch does not establish that identification (ev_krishna_dwarka, ev_sachi_sri, ev_dhananjaya).
Vasudeva, Kesava and Vishnu are not equated with one another or with Krishna in the supplied passages (ev_subhadra, ev_agni, ev_kesava_vishnu). Sakra is not equated with Indra (ev_sakra, ev_indra).

Sakuni is explicitly Duryodhana's maternal uncle (ev_sakuni). The available relationship types cannot encode this uncle relationship; no unmentioned mother or additional sibling relationship has been generated.

Vyasa is called the grandfather of the Pandavas (ev_vyasa_birth), and both grandfather and great-grandfather of Janamejaya (ev_vyasa_grandfather, ev_vyasa_greatgrandfather). These generational claims cannot be represented directly with the available relationship types, and the wording differs for Janamejaya.

Saunaka's Bhrigu and Pramati ancestry, Janamejaya's Bharata ancestry, and continuation of Santanu's line lack complete intervening parentage (ev_sauti_ancestry, ev_saunaka_sauti, ev_bharata, ev_vyasa_begot). No immediate parent relationships have been inferred from these ancestry claims.

Astika's sons and grandsons and Kartikeya's rearing mothers are undifferentiated groups (ev_astika_brahmana, ev_divine_family); no individual records have been generated from them. The collective snake speakers and the phrase 'the foremost of the chief snakes assembled together' do not unambiguously identify an additional individual snake.

The woodland Rakshasa and 'the Rakshasa he slew' are treated as the same unnamed referent through the paragraph's contextual anaphora (ev_woodland_rakshasa, ev_hidimva). Its gender is not stated; 'he slew' refers to Bhima.

Ghatotkacha is born of Hidimva, but Bhima is not expressly identified as his parent in this batch (ev_hidimva). Hidimva's own species is not stated. Dundubha's and Garuda's species are also not stated (ev_dundubha, ev_agni_gifts).

The Sachi-Indra and Sri-Krishna spouse relationships are provisional because the passage compares unions in a marriage context without expressly calling those figures husband and wife (ev_subhadra, ev_sachi_sri).
Parvati and Mahadeva's union supports Kartikeya's divine parentage, but the passage does not state a marriage between them (ev_divine_family).

Brahma may denote metaphysical reality rather than a narrative individual (ev_supreme_brahma, ev_union_brahma), so its entity record is provisional. Identity with the personally phrased Brahman in ev_brahman is not established.

Sun and Earth are retained provisionally because astronomical comparisons and feminine personification do not clearly establish narrative personhood or deity status (ev_sun_earth, ev_rahu). Earth's gender annotation records the passage's personification.

The young monarch, his queen, their possible son or daughter, generic readers, hearers, embryos, servants and other hypothetical persons on page 63 are illustrative categories rather than identifiable narrative individuals. No entities have been generated for them. Named rivers, mountains, texts, weapons, rites and abstract instructional domains are not individually depicted as narrative beings in this batch.

matches.reason: Both identify the Brahmana born of Jaratkaru who saved the snakes from Janamejaya's sacrifice; the existing evidence includes the same account of his eventual death.
The same protective remembrance names Artiman alongside Astika and Sunitha.
The same protective remembrance names Sunitha alongside Astika and Artiman.
Parentage from Parikshit and the snake-sacrifice distinguish this king from the other Janamejayas.
The existing text explicitly gives Ugrasrava the name Sauti; both are the framing narrator addressed by Saunaka as son of Suta.
Both invoke Bhrigu as the ancestor of Sauti's framing listener through addresses identifying the listener with Bhrigu's race.
Both identify Pramati as Ruru's father; the existing account also has that father relate the requested history.
Ruru is explicitly Pramati's son in both accounts.
Both identify Saunaka as the framing listener questioning Sauti, whom he addresses as son of Suta.
The Krishna-Dwaipayana identity, Bharata composition, parentage from Parasara, and begetting of Pandu, Dhritarashtra and Vidura corroborate this match.
The distinctive birth agrees: a maiden bears Krishna-Dwaipayana by Parasara. The existing account identifies that mother as Satyavati, also called Gandhakali.
Both identify Parasara as the progenitor of Dwaipayana Vyasa, distinguishing him from the serpent Parasara.
Pandu belongs to the same three children begotten by Krishna-Dwaipayana and is identified as a parent of the Pandava Bhima.
The king begotten with Pandu and Vidura by Krishna-Dwaipayana, and identified as Duryodhana's parent, matches the existing Kuru king.
His membership in the three children begotten by Krishna-Dwaipayana and his protection of the Pandavas against the lac-house designs corroborate the existing Vidura.
Both identify Santanu as Bhishma's parent.
The deity's union with Sachi corroborates the existing Indra explicitly addressed as Sachi's consort.
Both identify Bharata as the progenitor of the dynasty containing Janamejaya, the son of Parikshit.
Both identify Vyasa's disciple reciting the Bharata to Janamejaya at the snake-sacrifice under Krishna-Dwaipayana's direction.
The deceased father of the returning Pandavas matches the existing account of Pandu's five sons being introduced to the Kauravas after his death.
Dhritarashtra's son who persecutes the Pandavas matches the existing Duryodhana's parentage and conflict.
Both place Karna among Duryodhana's advisers supporting his persecution and destruction of the Pandavas.
His counsel to Duryodhana and participation in the dice scheme against Yudhishthira match the existing gambling antagonist, distinguishing him from the snake Sakuni.
The Bhimasena name, parentage from Kunti, and marriage to Hidimva corroborate the existing Pandava Bhima.
Kunti's parentage of Bhima and Arjuna agrees with the existing account of her offspring.
The existing Indra record lists Sakra as an alias and describes Sakra as a protector of creatures; CURRENT likewise presents Sakra as the heavenly guardian of the world of men.
Both identify Purochana as the individual burned in the house of lac.
The same passage identifies her as Bhima's wife and sister of the Rakshasa he slew.
The existing evidence contains the same birth from Hidimva in the account of her marriage to Bhima.
The demon's slaying in the Pandavas' Adi narrative corroborates the existing synopsis of the destruction of the Asura Vaka.
Both identify Draupadi as the common wife of the five Pandavas.
The explicit identification of Bhishma as Santanu's son corroborates the existing parentage.
The existing text explicitly equates Pritha with Kunti; CURRENT's parentage of Bhima and Arjuna corroborates that identity.
His parentage from Kunti and marriage to Subhadra in Dwaravati agree with the existing Arjuna's family and marriage narrative.
Nakula is explicitly one of Madri's two sons alongside Sahadeva in both accounts.
Sahadeva is explicitly one of Madri's two sons alongside Nakula in both accounts.
CURRENT's solar luminary in an eclipse comparison corresponds to the Sun in the existing eclipse comparison concerning Kasyapa's fame.
Explicit parentage from Dharma and siblinghood with Arjuna corroborate the existing Pandava Yudhishthira.
Krishna appears in the same Dwaravati narrative of Arjuna obtaining Subhadra that existing evidence associates with Krishna and Subhadra.
The existing text identifies Vasudeva with Krishna and calls Krishna Subhadra's brother; CURRENT explicitly identifies Vasudeva as Subhadra's sibling.
Her marriage to Arjuna in Dwaravati and sibling relationship with Vasudeva agree with the existing marriage account.
CURRENT's union comparison pairs Sachi with Indra, corroborating the existing identification as Indra's consort.
Both identify Agni as gratified by Arjuna through the burning of Khandava; the Gandiva association also agrees.
Existing evidence explicitly identifies Kesava as Krishna, and CURRENT places Kesava alongside Arjuna as his assistant in the Khandava episode.
The distinctive chariot-standard motif corroborates the existing Garuda placed on a chariot flagstaff.
Both identify the Asura rescued by Arjuna who builds the Pandavas' celestial palace or assembly hall.
His connection to Draupadi in the same account of her marriage to five husbands corroborates the existing Drupada's marriage-related concern.
Both identify Madri as the parent of Nakula and Sahadeva.
